title.en: Verbs and expressions followed by -ing after a preposition

summary.en: After a **preposition** the verb is always an **-ing form**: _interested **in learning**_, _before **leaving**_, _without **asking**_, _thank you for **helping**_. This includes the preposition **to** in phrases such as _look forward **to seeing**_ and _be used **to working**_. Some fixed expressions also take **-ing**: _there's no point in_, _it's no use_, _it's worth_, _have difficulty (in)_.
summary.es: En español usamos el infinitivo después de una preposición («antes de salir», «sin preguntar»). En inglés es siempre la forma en -ing: _before leaving_, _without asking_. Ojo con **to**: en _look forward to_ es una preposición, así que sigue -ing.

form: Verb + preposition + **-ing**: _insist on paying_, _apologise for being_, _succeed in finding_
Adjective + preposition + **-ing**: _tired of waiting_, _capable of doing_, _fed up with queuing_
Fixed expressions: _there's no point in_ / _it's no use_ / _it's worth_ / _have difficulty (in)_ / _spend time_ + **-ing**
Test for **to**: if you can put a noun or _it_ after it (_I'm looking forward to it_), it is a preposition and takes **-ing**

uses.text: **After any preposition**: _Check the oven before **leaving**. She got the job by **impressing** the manager._
**After verb + preposition**: _He insisted on **paying**. They're thinking of **moving**. We succeeded in **booking** a table._
**After adjective + preposition**: _I'm tired of **hearing** the same excuse. She's good at **explaining** difficult ideas._
**Phrases with to as a preposition**: _I look forward to **seeing** you. He's not used to **driving** on the left. She objected to **working** at weekends._

note.en: Compare: _I want to see you_ (to + infinitive) and _I look forward to seeing you_ (preposition + -ing).
note.es: Compara: _I want to see you_ (to + infinitivo) y _I look forward to seeing you_ (preposición + -ing).

uses.text: **Fixed expressions**: _There's no point in **arguing**. It's no use **waiting**. It's worth **trying**. We had difficulty **finding** the house._

mistakes.wrong: Before to leave, please sign the register.
mistakes.right: Before leaving, please sign the register.

why.en: After a preposition we use the -ing form, never to + infinitive.
why.es: Tras una preposición va -ing, no «to + infinitivo» (aunque en español digamos «antes de salir»).

mistakes.wrong: I look forward to see you next week.
mistakes.right: I look forward to seeing you next week.

why.en: In look forward to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
why.es: En _look forward to_, **to** es preposición: va seguida de -ing.

mistakes.wrong: It's worth to visit the old town.
mistakes.right: It's worth visiting the old town.

why.en: Worth is followed directly by an -ing form.

mistakes.wrong: She left without to say anything.

why.en: Without is a preposition, so it takes -ing.
why.es: «Sin decir nada» se traduce con -ing: _without saying_.

mistakes.wrong: We had difficulty to find a taxi.
mistakes.right: We had difficulty finding a taxi.

why.en: After have difficulty (or trouble) we use -ing, with or without in.
why.es: Tras _have difficulty / trouble_ va -ing, no infinitivo.

examples.en: Before signing the contract, read every page carefully.
examples.es: Antes de firmar el contrato, lee todas las páginas con atención.

examples.en: He left the party without saying goodbye.
examples.es: Se fue de la fiesta sin despedirse.

examples.en: She's interested in training as a physiotherapist.
I'm looking forward to seeing my cousins again.
examples.es: Tengo ganas de volver a ver a mis primos.

examples.en: They insisted on paying for the whole meal.
She apologised for being late and explained what had happened.
There's no point in arguing with him; he never changes his mind.
examples.es: No tiene sentido discutir con él; nunca cambia de opinión.

examples.en: It's worth booking early if you want a window seat.
We had difficulty finding the entrance to the car park.
By working evenings, he saved enough for a deposit.
I'm fed up with waiting for the bus in the rain.

practice.prompt: I'm tired of ___ the same answer every day.

explanation.en: Of is a preposition, so the verb takes the -ing form.

practice.prompt: He walked out of the meeting without ___ a word.

explanation.en: Without is a preposition and is followed by -ing.

practice.prompt: Is it worth ___ the museum if we only have an hour?

explanation.en: Worth is followed by an -ing form.

practice.prompt: We had difficulty ___ a parking space near the station.
I'm really looking forward to ___ the new team next month.

explanation.en: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
